status: Evaluation closed: reject this SQL-coverage integration for current production; preserve feasible native-column storage as an experimental option.

decision.reason: Measured whole-worker CPU and I/O/cache costs are excessive for the requested joint CPU/memory improvement. Exact representation and export feasibility passed; rejection is of this implementation, not Arrow/DuckDB feasibility in general.
decision.parent_decision: Root agreed not to activate the full60 SQL-coverage chain on 2026-10-10 after the exact fifteen-input probe.
decision.production_change: None from this storage evaluation. Retain the clean validated R calculation and ordinary self-contained QS2 output; finish the separately evaluated R output orchestration only through its own acceptance gates.

environment.packages: Existing HiDEF-seq 3.0 SIF: R 4.4.2, Arrow 18.1.0.1, DuckDB 1.3.1, DBI 1.2.3, dplyr 1.1.4, dbplyr 2.5.0. No package/SIF changes.
environment.threads: Matched burden/export replay arms use 1 CPU, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1. Production burden allocation is 2 CPUs; these numbers do not replace production-pipeline accounting.
environment.source_variants: One-input full-path smoke uses full-task-v3; five/fifteen use full-task-v5 with separately proven raw factor/empty-contract repairs. Scientific helper baseline remains 358e4bf. The unexecuted v6 changes only the finish_coverage connection memory setting.

representation_and_operations.operation_scope: Two tables, three real sizes (5/15/60), seven operations, two native backends. Includes stable global distinct, duplicate-multiplicity joins and list values. Full result types, factor levels, names, attributes and order match R.
representation_and_operations.coverage_specimens: 1,752 retained Rle/RleList specimens containing 1,760 Rles; full specimen reconstruction and 1,760 interior windows per backend exact. Whole aggregation is separately tested.
representation_and_operations.arrow_limit: Installed Arrow direct joins carrying list payload failed; the explicit native scalar-row-ID join followed by requested list-column fetch passed exactly. This is a measured materialization path, not native list-payload join support.

operation_cpu_boundary_example.scope: Whole suite includes startup, initial input read, result collection/save and teardown; native prestaging is excluded, while R loads its QS fixture. Timed operations start from resident R. This favors DuckDB over Arrow for the tested disk-backed path, not DuckDB over already-resident R operations.

representation_and_operations.examples: Preserved operations-v2.R and operations-v2-finalCalls / operations-v2-germlineVariantCalls contain runnable whole-table examples and exact result receipts.
representation_and_operations.arrow_full_burden_recommendation: No full Arrow burden rewrite is warranted by these results. Arrow remains technically feasible; its tested operations are slower than DuckDB and add the list-join materialization boundary.

burden_limits: Native-first sequential pairs use the same allocation and 1 CPU at each size; only one order was measured, so node/cache carryover and co-located work remain caveats. One-input jobs were separate allocations.

Approximately 20.32 GiB is the observed whole-process peak at 1/5/15 inputs, not a proven floor, bound or attribution to input loading. Cumulative HWM does not identify the peak source. Whole input QS objects are still loaded one at a time.

All twenty backed and ordinary-assembled QS components passed at 1/5/15. The eight BEDs and both sets of own indexes were scientifically compared only for one input. Five/fifteen file sizes alone are not content proof.

No complete sixty-input SQL-backed burden worker ran. The planned chain was canceled while verified unstarted; v6 remains disabled. No full60 upstream or actual strict60-to-four-source consumer acceptance is claimed.
one_input_complete_scope: Complete burden code path with one actual chunk, twenty components, eight coverage BEDs and own indexes, single-source eighteen final components and 140 scientific files, including ordinary consumer from assembled burden. These are measured complete smoke path sums, not full-size performance claims.
fifteen_input_memory_interpretation: Process peak is essentially unchanged; candidate sampled current memory/file cache is much higher. Counters are non-simultaneous sampled lower bounds; memory.peak is cumulative for the paired job and cache carries over. This does not demonstrate a job-memory saving.

larger_pool.effective_setting: 8.0 GiB (8,589,934,592 bytes), threads 1; same source-extracted SQL/schema and read-only original DB.
larger_pool.interpretation: The setting is feasible and exact. Its isolated query time cannot be divided into the broader 512 MB phase to claim causal speedup. Temporary-file use persists, with a sampled 46.735 GB logical maximum; this is occupied space, not cumulative bytes written.

conditional_cost_model.limits: Illustration only: holding all old non-reduction work fixed while replacing the broader old phase with the narrower isolated new query is not a measured full worker, prediction, lower bound or causal setting comparison. It offers no credible demonstrated joint CPU/memory win warranting a long full60 run.

four_source_exports.scope: Starts from four already accepted ordinary burden outputs, stages them into native storage, then compares ordinary and backed consumers. Does not prove all four upstream native-storage burden calculations.

acceptance.comparison: R identical() covers types, attributes, names, list cells and order; TSV exact bytes, established PDF canonical comparison and VCF fileDate-only normalization, own TBI rebuilt validity. Validation cost is separate.

portable_final_data.scope: Portable final data closure only, not total pipeline retained storage. Ordinary pipelines may retain burden intermediates; scratch peaks are separate.

four_source_exports.interpretation: Consumer-only process RSS falls from 43.02 to 6.59 GiB, at +34.18% CPU. Ordinary final assembly returns peak to 40.37 GiB and increases consumer-plus-assembly CPU to 2630.584613 s (+82.08% versus native), before migration. First-use all-four migration plus that path costs 4810.778325 CPU s. A small final QS is not standalone; complete backing closure is required.

cost_accounting: Native burden includes ordinary QS serialization; backed burden saves a small QS and backing DB. Mode A must add ordinary twenty-component assembly before an ordinary consumer.

Mode B may feed its backed burden directly to a backed consumer. Final eighteen-component standalone assembly is optional and distinct from ordinary burden assembly; do not require or double-count both without that path.

If an actual strict60 backed source were used, migrate only the other three accepted ordinary sources: 390.526223 CPU s, 835.997799 summed wall s, maximum process RSS 16,842,724 KiB. This path was not run.
All validation, hash/guard wrapper overhead, failed attempts and optional compaction are separately recorded. Known artifact censuses report retained bytes, not peak scratch or cumulative I/O.

Frozen burden DBs retain events/dimensions. A separate full1 fresh-DB copy reduced DB bytes from 332,673,024 to 214,970,368 with all20 exact, costing 5.752569 CPU s; DROP/CHECKPOINT alone did not shrink. Old/new copies coexist, so compaction is neither free nor guaranteed by DROP.

maintenance.meaning: Unique current integration only, excluding historical copies, test/launch controls and copied existing scientific fragment. Dense physical line count understates complexity. No generic per-cell serialization framework or new C++ was built, but the complete storage/export lifecycle is substantially larger than the small name/type adapter.
maintenance.new_non_R_logic: Custom SQL through existing DuckDB/DBI handles event reduction and native ordering/distinct/query operations. Production calculation remains R; this SQL prototype is not production-integrated.
requirements: Native schema and append promotion must preserve factor-level unions, types, explicit NA levels, list values, column names, row IDs and stable first-occurrence ordering.
Small QS manifests preserve ordinary prototypes, metadata, source ordering, coverage Seqinfo and native table references; small QS alone is not a standalone result.

Workflow cache and publish declarations must retain the complete backing closure, with reliable relative paths, completion checks, restart/recovery behavior and format-version policy. These are not production integrated.
Native reduction, query ordering and existing R scientific arithmetic boundaries must remain synchronized with pipeline changes; SQL is a new non-R dependency in maintained logic.
Each DuckDB connection has its own 512MB setting; the four-source path opens eight connections and this setting does not bound total process or job memory.
Project scratch, transaction/checkpoint lifetime, cleanup of temporary event tables, optional fresh-database compaction and old/new database coexistence require explicit lifecycle management.
Public readers currently use the production package load order for some unqualified dplyr verbs; a production API should remove this session-order dependency.
remaining_limits: Actual strict LIB1 symmetric-barcode burden configuration is tested; unsupported orientations error explicitly. Generalizing all valid production configurations is unfinished.

Whole input QS objects are still loaded one at a time. The burden finish phase still materializes all processed TSV/unique TSV/VCF/unique VCF tables for unchanged R calculations. Overall memory is not bounded.
Ordinary burden and final-output assembly intentionally materialize whole ordinary R results, and ordinary downstream consumers retain their existing whole-object allocation.

Four-source consumer feasibility stages accepted ordinary outputs; the eventual actual strict60 path calculates only the strict nuclear source with native storage and separately migrates the other three accepted ordinary outputs.

The narrow exact native-column attributes adapter is small; the surrounding storage, coverage reduction, streaming export, materialization and lifecycle integration is substantially larger and should be weighed independently.

r_coverage_with_duckdb_calls.verdict: Technically feasible and not ruled out by exactness, but a new unvalidated integration.
r_coverage_with_duckdb_calls.plausible_benefit: Avoid SQL event expansion/spill while storing accumulated raw call columns natively. Existing R coverage-only and raw-call append proofs support plausibility, not the combined result.
r_coverage_with_duckdb_calls.necessary_work: Compose coverage manifests/readers/track mappings, native call contracts, ordinary assembly, temporary-file lifetime and restart/cleanup; validate all configurations and scientific external products. The old R coverage adapter/reducer is about 455 physical lines with bypass/fallback branches and pre-358 scientific closure, so it is not a drop-in finalized path.
r_coverage_with_duckdb_calls.arithmetic: The earlier grouped R reducer is exact in its tested bounded nonnegative-integer domain. General double/fractional coverage may depend on addition order; do not assume reassociation is exact. Current clipping/circular/unknown-length/NA/orientation and metadata cases need a deliberate coherent implementation, not a narrowed production contract or retained fallback.
r_coverage_with_duckdb_calls.remaining_allocations: One entire filtered input QS per step, merge operands/processed call tables, full ordinary burden/final QS assembly and ordinary consumer allocations remain. No bounded whole-pipeline claim.
r_coverage_with_duckdb_calls.recommendation: Do not start another rewrite or allocation for current finalization. Preserve as a future option if a concrete small proposal can credibly improve both CPU and memory beyond the validated R path.

few_qs_temporary_handoff.verdict: A simpler R phase handoff can preserve ordinary serialization and may reduce concurrent residency. It still requires measured I/O, process startup, exact global transforms and full standalone assembly.
few_qs_temporary_handoff.scope: The separately evaluated output-only R orchestration is the appropriate near-term path if its own gates pass. It does not validate an upstream R-coverage/DuckDB hybrid. No additional experiment is proposed here.

closed_status.full60: No active allocation; prior unstarted jobs canceled with receipts, successor disabled and not to be activated.
closed_status.historical_failures: Initial package/metadata errors, unsupported Arrow native list join, prototype reference lookup failure, comparator OOM and inventory/SIF guard failures remain preserved with their actual failed or unexecuted status. No comparison was waived.
closed_status.remaining_integration: Production adoption, all-configuration native storage support and full60 SQL-backed upstream are intentionally not completed because this implementation is rejected for current production.
